from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Discrete data often looks like histograms.",
            "Imagine shrinking the bars until they disappear.",
            "A smooth curve emerges as the limit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Discrete to Continuous Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        # Fix: Manim BarChart labels default to Tex; use plain strings or set tex_template for better stability
        hist = BarChart(values=[1, 3, 4, 3, 1], bar_names=["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"], y_range=[0, 5, 1])
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 4 * np.exp(-(x - 3)**2 / 2), x_range=[0, 6])
        
        # Setup visuals on grid
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        # Position objects directly for animation
        hist.scale(0.5).next_to(axes.get_origin(), ORIGIN)
        curve.set_stroke(color=YELLOW, width=4).scale(0.5).next_to(axes.get_origin(), ORIGIN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(hist))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeOut(hist), FadeIn(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(curve.animate.set_stroke(color=GOLD))
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 6], color=YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        self.play(Create(area))
        label = Text("Total Probability = 1", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "PDF represents probability density, not probability.",
            "Think of density like gold dust.",
            "Probability is the area under the curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the PDF", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axis setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "tip_shape": StealthTip}
        ).scale(0.6)
        y_label = Text("Density", font_size=20).next_to(axes.y_axis.get_top(), RIGHT)
        x_label = Text("Value", font_size=20).next_to(axes.x_axis.get_right(), UP)
        
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, y_label, x_label)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group, "A1", "D6")
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(y_label), Write(x_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        func = lambda x: 3 * np.exp(-(x - 3)**2 / 0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[1, 5], color="#00CED1")
        self.play(Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Highlight point x
        x_val = 3
        point_x = Dot(axes.c2p(x_val, 0), color=RED)
        label_x = MathTex("x", font_size=24).next_to(point_x, DOWN)
        
        f_x_point = Dot(axes.c2p(x_val, func(x_val)), color=RED)
        label_fx = MathTex("f(x)", font_size=24).next_to(f_x_point, UP)
        dashed_line = DashedLine(point_x.get_center(), f_x_point.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point_x), Write(label_x))
        self.play(Create(dashed_line), FadeIn(f_x_point), Write(label_fx))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Highlight area
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[2.5, 3.5], color=YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        self.play(Create(area))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Robot Battery Example", [
            "Consider a robot with variable battery life.",
            "We model this with a specific function.",
            "The probability is the area between points."
        ])
        
        # Define the PDF (simple triangle/trapezoid for demo)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 2], y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1], axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'D6')

        self.add(pdf)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        # Shade region [4, 6]
        shaded_area = axes.get_area(pdf, x_range=[4, 6], color=RED, opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(shaded_area))
        
        label = Text("Probability of failure", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(label))
        
        integral = MathTex(r"\int_{4}^{6} f(x) \, dx", font_size=24).set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(integral, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(integral))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Key Takeaways", [
            "Area under the curve equals probability.",
            "Single point probability is always zero.",
            "Normalization ensures total area is one."
        ])
        
        # Define graphics
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5], x_length=4, y_length=3, axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-(x-2)**2 / 0.5), x_range=[0, 4])
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[1, 3], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        formula = MathTex(r"P(a < X < b) = \int_{a}^{b} f(x)dx", font_size=28)
        norm_text = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)dx = 1", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(axes, curve, area), 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area), Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 0), color=RED)
        point_label = Text("P(X=x) = 0", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(point_label, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeOut(area), FadeOut(point), FadeOut(point_label), FadeOut(formula))
        self.place_at_grid(norm_text, 'C3')
        self.play(Write(norm_text))
        
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly recall discrete probability (histograms). Transition to continuous variables by imagining shrinking histogram bin widths toward zero. Introduce the transition from 'bars' to a 'smooth curve'.
sections.example: Visual transition: A histogram of height measurements gradually becomes a smooth bell-shaped line as we collect millions of data points.

sections.title: Defining the Probability Density Function (PDF)
sections.content: Define PDF (f(x)). Crucial realization: f(x) is NOT probability; it is density. Explain that probability corresponds to the 'area under the curve' (the integral).
sections.example: Analogy: If density is a cloud of gold dust, the probability is the amount of gold inside a specific box, not the height of the cloud at one point.

sections.title: Core Properties & Visual Constraints
sections.content: Highlight two mathematical laws: 1) f(x) >= 0 (no negative probability density); 2) Total area under the curve must equal 1 (the 'Total Certainty' rule).
sections.example: Visual animation: A 'Total Probability' container filling up with water to exactly 1 liter. If we stretch the curve, it must compress in height to keep the volume constant.

sections.title: Applied Example: The Robot's Battery Life
sections.content: Demonstrate finding the probability of an event using a specific PDF. Calculate the likelihood of a robot battery dying between 4 and 6 hours by shading the area under the curve.
sections.example: A robot named 'Bolt' has a battery life modeled by a specific function. We shade the region between x=4 and x=6 to visualize the probability Bolt will stop working during that window.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
sections.content: Recap: Area = Probability. Remind that f(x) at a single point is 0, but the integral over an interval gives the likelihood. Close with the concept of normalization.
sections.example: Quick 'Flashcard' screen: A summary graphic showing a shaded area on a plot with the formula P(a < X < b) = ∫[a,b] f(x)dx.
